subject: CS handoff: cost & performance ops plan for Orchid AI
messages:
From: Danielle Park <dpark@orchid-ai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@orchid-ai.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CS handoff: cost & performance ops plan for Orchid AI

Thanks Evelyn — excited to get this moving. Two quick asks before the handoff call:

1) Can you share a short checklist of the tuning knobs you typically adjust during onboarding (batching, cache, quantization profiles, routing)?
2) We can provide a one-week sample of production traffic (anonymized). Which format do you prefer?

We’d like cost targets ~35% lower than our current self-hosted baseline while keeping median latency under 250ms for short prompts.

—Danielle
Product Lead, Orchid AI

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@orchid-ai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CS handoff: cost & performance ops plan for Orchid AI

Hi Danielle — thanks for the targets, very helpful. Attaching our 1-page "cost + perf tuning checklist" (redwood-cost-tuning-checklist.pdf) and a short template for the sample traffic (orchid-sample-traffic.json). High level notes below:

- Batching: aim for dynamic batching with max batch window of 20-40ms for interactive flows; target batch size 8–16 for short prompts to keep p50 latency sub-250ms.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and templates; we expect 40–60% hit rate for chat assistants with templated context.
- Quantization profile: we typically evaluate int8 first (good quality/size tradeoff). If you need further cost savings, test int4 for non-critical routes — evaluate on the same eval set.
- Routing policies: recommend primary route to rdx-8b-int8 for cost+latency balance; fallback to rdx-3b-int8 for heavy bursts and rdx-8b-int4 if cost takes priority over highest fidelity.

Next steps:
- Can you drop the anonymized 7-day traffic by EOD 10/06? (we'll use it to run a simulated profiler)
- Schedule a 45-minute handoff call next week for tuning and mutual action plan. Dev will lead the technical portion.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Amit Rao <amit@orchid-ai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Danielle Park <dpark@orchid-ai.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CS handoff: cost & performance ops plan for Orchid AI

Thanks Evelyn — we'll export logs. Two clarifications:

- Our short prompts are ~12–30 tokens; long form is up to 800 tokens. Should we expect different tuning per route?
- Any preferred format for latency SLAs in the MAP (mutual action plan)?

Also copying procurement for contract timing.

—Amit
Engineering Manager, Orchid AI

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit@orchid-ai.com>, Danielle Park <dpark@orchid-ai.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CS handoff: cost & performance ops plan for Orchid AI

Hi Amit — short answers here:

- Yes, route-based tuning recommended. Suggest two logical routes: 
  * "interactive" (<= 50 tokens): low-latency profile — smaller max batch, higher priority routing to rdx-8b-int8, aggressive prefix caching.
  * "longform" (> 50 tokens): throughput-first — larger batch windows, prefer rdx-13b-int8 or rdx-8b-int4 depending on quality needs.

- MAP SLA suggestions (we can surface in the doc): p50 latency targets per route (interactive <250ms, longform <900ms), cost-per-1k-token target, and cache hit-rate improvement goal (e.g., +30% from baseline).

I'll prep a short routing + profile recommendation to share on the call. Also, please include a sample of templates you use — those help caching decisions.

Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Park <dpark@orchid-ai.com>

—Danielle

Thanks — got the CSV and drive link. Call confirmed for 2026-10-08 10:00 PT (45 minutes). Agenda below:

1) Quick intro + success metrics (5m)
2) Review sample traffic and initial profiler snapshots (10m)
3) Batching & queueing parameters we recommend (Dev) (12m)
4) Cache strategy and template mapping (8m)
5) Quantization profile tradeoffs (int8 vs int4) and rollout plan (5m)
6) Routing policy: primary/fallback and canary approach (3m)

Pre-read: redwood-cost-tuning-checklist.pdf; please review quantization section if you expect to test int4 on staging.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Park <dpark@orchid-ai.com>, Amit Rao <amit@orchid-ai.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CS handoff: cost & performance ops plan for Orchid AI

Following the call notes — quick summary and next steps:

- Initial profiler results: interactive route p50 ~220ms, current batching giving average batch size 4. We can push target batch size to 10 with a 30ms batching window and expect ~20% cost reduction without hurting p95 too much.
- Cache: mapped 6 templates to the prefix cache — predicted hit rate +28% in first pass.
- Quantization: agreed to run A/B on staging: rdx-8b-int8 vs rdx-8b-int4 for non-critical flows; if quality delta >2% we will rollback int4.
- Routing policy: primary rdx-8b-int8; burst fallback to rdx-3b-int8; emergency cost-cut route rdx-8b-int4 behind a canary flag.

Action items:
- Dev: create canary flag and rollout playbook (due 10/13).
- Evelyn: update MAP with SLA rows and attach the screenshots from profiler (due 10/10).
- Orchid: confirm procurement timeline and sign-off.

Nice work team.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
